messages:
maya: Quick Q — what's the canonical embeddings endpoint contract when clients send mixed inputs and some inputs exceed model token limits? planning a migration for our vector store.

jesse: Endpoint expects inputs as an array of strings, or an array of objects with an `input` field. We do NOT accept nested lists (no list-of-lists). Keep it flat.

kai: To add: when an item exceeds the per-input token limit we either truncate or reject depending on `truncation_policy`. Current default = `truncate`. If you set `truncation_policy=reject` you get a 413 with a per-item error. We also support `include_truncation=true` to surface which items were trimmed.

maya: Here's the minimal request I tried (python):
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-2-small",
  "inputs": ["short sentence", "<very long text...>"]
}
```

jesse: And the shape we return (per-item metadata included if requested):
```json
{
  "model":"redwood-embed-2-small",
  "data":[
    {"index":0, "embedding":[0.012,-0.003,0.091], "truncated":false},
    {"index":1, "embedding":[0.110,-0.220,0.005], "truncated":true}
  ],
  "usage":{"input_tokens":1234}
}
```

kai: Practical limits (model-specific): `max_inputs_per_request = 1024` for embed-2-small, `max_input_tokens_per_item = 8192`. If you hit the tokens limit we follow the configured `truncation_policy`. Batching is automatic on the server, so don't pass >1024 inputs in one call — you'll get 413.

ciara: Back-compat note: switching default from `truncate` -> `reject` would be breaking. We're keeping default=`truncate` for a release cycle, but adding a warning header `X-Embedding-Truncation: warn` for affected requests.

embeds-bot: NOTE: Deprecation/compat plan published in RFC-789. New header and `include_truncation` opt-in will roll out next month. See https://redwood.ai/rfc/789 :thumbsup:

maya: OK — I'll update our ingest pipeline to request `include_truncation=true` and handle `index` + `truncated` flags. Filing a small SDK PR and will add tests for shape and ordering.

ciara: thanks — ping @eng-docs to add an example for the object-form input (e.g., `{ "input": "...", "metadata": {...} }`) and a note about per-item `truncated` boolean.
